newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Caltex Sri Lanka unit to begin trading on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Sri Lanka unit to begin trading on Monday.

text.p: Shares in Lanka Lubricants Ltd, the Sri Lankan subsidiary of oil company Caltex, will begin trading on the Colombo stock exchange on Monday, the exchange said on Wednesday.
Lanka Lubricants publicly offered 11.7 million shares, or 39 percent of its issued capital, at 50 rupees per share in July but the public took up only about 18 percent of the offer.
The balance was taken by underwriters Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka Ltd and the state-owned Bank of Ceylon.
Lanka Lubricants shares will be classified under the manufacturing sector, the exchange said in a statement. Caltex is a joint venture of Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc

Brokers said the lukewarm public response to Lanka Lubricants shares was due to the bearish stock market mood in July when the all share index fell below 600 points for the first time in over three years.
The state sold a 51 percent stake to Caltex in 1992.
Ten percent of the company's issued capital was given free to employees in November 1995 under the country's privatisation formula.
The public offer was the portion that was in state hands.
